column2: On the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Suckling makes unlawful what birth makes unlawful.” Recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

The Noble Qurʾān has made unlawful foster mothers and foster sisters, in the saying of the Exalted: “…and your [foster] mothers who nursed you, and your sisters through nursing…” [al-Nisāʾ 4:23]; and the Sunnah has come, with this hadith and others of like meaning, [establishing] that suckling makes unlawful what birth makes unlawful.

So everything that is unlawful through lineage, its like is unlawful through suckling. When a child is suckled by a woman, she becomes his foster mother, and her father and grandfathers become his foster fathers,
her mother and grandmothers his foster mothers, her brothers his foster maternal uncles, and her sisters his foster maternal aunts;

and her children, whether from one husband or several, become his foster siblings. Likewise, the husband of the nursing woman, from whose milk he suckled, becomes his foster father, his father and grandfathers his foster fathers, his mother and grandmothers his foster mothers,

his brothers and sisters his foster paternal uncles and aunts, his children from several wives his foster siblings, and his wives his foster stepmothers. And so with everything that is unlawful through lineage: its like is unlawful through suckling.
The printed text reads يحرم بالولادة مثله (“its like is unlawful through birth”), evidently for يحرم بالرضاعة مثله (“…through suckling”), as the rest of the paragraph shows.

The suckling by which unlawfulness is established is five sucklings or more, within the first two years. If it is fewer than five, unlawfulness is not established by it; nor is unlawfulness established by the suckling of an adult.

What has come in the story of Sālim, the freed slave of Abū Ḥudhayfah (recorded by Muslim, 1453), is restricted to him and does not extend to anyone else. What makes clear that the suckling of an adult does not count—
since it does not nourish—is that any woman who wanted to be rid of her husband could express from her breast into a cup the equivalent of five sucklings or more,
give it to her husband to drink without his knowing, and then say to him afterwards: I am not lawful for you,
because you are my foster son.
The perfection of the Sharīʿah and its containing general, universal principles, as has come in this hadith.
Every woman who is unlawful through lineage, her counterpart through suckling is unlawful.
